title: Graded-Relevance Composed Multimodal Retrieval for E-commerce Visual Search at Scale
title_zh: 面向大规模电商视觉搜索的分级相关性组合多模态检索
abstract_en: Visual search on large e-commerce catalogs must serve both "similarity" queries that ask for items resembling an uploaded image and "modifier" queries that comprise an image and text describing a desired modification (e.g. a color change or style swap). The latter is the setting known as composed image retrieval (CIR). Existing CIR methods, however, treat relevance as binary and train on triplets with a single positive target - a poor fit for real catalogs where many candidates partially satisfy a user query and ranking across that partial-match spectrum drives the customer experience. We propose a methodology for training CIR retrievers on graded relevance, consisting of: (i) a VLM to curate training data, generating both queries (object detection + modifier synthesis) and 4-level relevance labels without manual annotation, (ii) an iterative relevance-feedback loop that expands the training set by mining hard negatives from the in-training retriever, and (iii) a hierarchy-aware angular objective to train the retriever directly on the graded labels rather than collapsing them to a binary split. We call this methodology GradCIR and instantiate it on a PaliGemma2 bi-encoder trained on 3.5M graded pairs curated from raw Walmart catalog data. A controlled graded-vs-binary ablation isolates the supervision granularity and shows lift of 4.9%-5.9% in NDCG@10. The same recipe applied to other multimodal encoders lifts early-fusion backbones by up to 8.5% NDCG@10. On the public FashionIQ benchmark, GradCIR (applied to PaliGemma2) reaches 0.6703 average recall when fine-tuned, slightly ahead of the strongest peer-reviewed supervised baseline we compare against, and matching or exceeding all published CLIP-L-class zero-shot CIR methods. The system is deployed in production at Walmart, where it's serving live visual-search user traffic.
abstract_zh: 大规模电商目录中的视觉搜索既包括根据上传图片寻找相似商品的“相似性”查询，也包括图片加文本修改描述的“修改器”查询，即组合图像检索（Composed Image Retrieval, CIR）。现有 CIR 方法通常将相关性视为二元标签，并使用仅含一个正样本的三元组训练，难以适应真实目录中大量仅部分满足查询的候选商品，以及由部分匹配程度决定的排序需求。本文提出 GradCIR，一套基于分级相关性训练 CIR 检索器的方法：首先利用视觉语言模型（VLM）自动生成查询和四级相关性标签，无需人工标注；随后通过相关性反馈迭代，从训练中的检索器挖掘困难负样本以扩充训练集；最后提出层次感知角度目标函数，直接利用分级标签训练检索器，而不是将其压缩为二元监督。作者基于 Walmart 原始商品目录构建了包含 350 万个分级样本对的数据集，并在 PaliGemma2 双编码器上实例化 GradCIR。受控实验表明，相比二元监督，分级监督使 NDCG@10 提升 4.9%–5.9%；将相同方案应用于其他多模态编码器时，早期融合骨干网络最高提升 8.5% NDCG@10。在公开 FashionIQ 基准上，经过微调的 GradCIR（基于 PaliGemma2）平均召回率达到 0.6703，略高于对比的最强同行评审监督基线，并达到或超过所有已发表的 CLIP-L 级零样本 CIR 方法。该系统已部署于 Walmart，服务真实视觉搜索流量。
key_points_zh: 针对真实电商目录中的部分匹配现象，将 CIR 相关性从二元标签扩展为四级分级标签。
利用 VLM 自动生成查询与相关性标注，并通过迭代相关性反馈挖掘困难负样本，降低人工数据构建成本。
提出层次感知角度目标函数，直接建模分级相关性，避免将不同程度的匹配粗略二值化。
在 Walmart 350 万分级样本上训练后，NDCG@10 相比二元监督提升 4.9%–5.9%；其他早期融合骨干最高提升 8.5%。
在 FashionIQ 上平均召回率达到 0.6703，并已部署至 Walmart 生产环境服务真实用户流量。

llm_assessment.comment: A strong production-grounded e-commerce visual-search paper that introduces graded relevance supervision and demonstrates substantial retrieval gains at Walmart scale.
llm_assessment.comment_zh: 这是一篇具有强生产落地背景的电商视觉搜索论文，通过 graded relevance 监督在沃尔玛规模上显著提升了检索效果。
